title: A second-generation M1-polarized CAR macrophage with antitumor efficacy
source: Show notes as published (Science TLDR ep. 26)
one_line: iPSC-derived macrophages engineered with a second-generation CAR containing a Toll/IL-1R (TIR) domain plus CD3ζ polarize to M1 and clear solid tumors in mouse models.
key_claims: CAR-iMACs were generated by differentiating induced pluripotent stem cells into macrophages and engineering them with chimeric antigen receptors, as an alternative to CAR T cells for solid tumors.
A second-generation CAR adding a TIR domain to CD3ζ outperformed the first-generation CD3ζ-only construct by activating the NFκB pathway.
The TIR domain drove polarization toward the pro-inflammatory M1 state.
Killing proceeded in two steps: induction of tumor cell apoptosis followed by clearance of debris via efferocytosis.
Complete tumor remission was reported in liver cancer mouse models, with mechanism supported by single-cell RNA sequencing, time-lapse microscopy and NFκB activation imaging.
limitations: Entirely preclinical: results come from cell culture and mouse models only.
CAR-iMACs show poor persistence and do not survive long in vivo.
Further research is required before human trials.
No human safety or efficacy data on antigen-specific targeting reducing side effects.
open_questions: Can CAR-iMAC persistence be extended in vivo, and does longer survival translate into durable responses?
Does efficacy hold in tumor types beyond the liver cancer models tested?
Would a first-in-human trial confirm the predicted low off-tumor toxicity of antigen-specific macrophage targeting?
Which combination partners best complement CAR-iMACs, and is the benefit additive or synergistic?
